subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Smurfing and Structuring
description: Learn Smurfing and Structuring in one minute.

hook.text: US banks must report cash deposits over $10,000. Criminals make dozens of $9,500 deposits instead.

buildup.text: Structuring means breaking large sums into smaller transactions to avoid triggering automatic reports.

discovery.text: Smurfs are recruited to make small deposits across many banks. Each transaction looks innocent alone.

twist.text: Structuring is itself a federal crime — even if the money is legitimate. The act of avoiding reports is illegal.

climax.text: Banks now use pattern detection to catch structuring. But with enough smurfs and banks, it still works.

punchline.text: $9,500 deposits. Dozens of banks. That's smurfing.

quiz.question: What is structuring in money laundering?
options: Breaking deposits into small amounts to avoid reporting thresholds
